claim: Didisheim, Ke, Kelly and Malamud (NBER w33012, Sept 2024): an SDF built from P random Fourier features of rank-standardized characteristics, S = [sin(gamma Z w), cos(gamma Z w)] with w ~ N(0, I) and gamma drawn per feature from {0.5, ..., 1.0}, factors F = N^-1/2 S'R and ridge Markowitz weights lambda(z) = (zI + E[FF'])^-1 E[F], earns out-of-sample SDF Sharpe ratios near 3.7 with high complexity and light shrinkage (360-month rolling window, monthly, 1993 onward), about 2.6 times the low-complexity models; the full-sample result is heavily influenced by microcaps, but mega- and large-cap-only SDFs still reach about 1.6 and 1.8, above FF6's 0.74. All gross of trading costs.
impact_on_spec: Defines M3: the same RFF form, gamma grid and ridge SDF estimator on our 23 slow inputs, weekly, expanding window, P = 4,000, ridge z chosen inside each training window; the SDF weight S lambda is the score fed to the unchanged v1.2 construction.
independent_replication: AQR Alternative Thinking 2024 Q4 reports the same 'virtue of complexity' pattern on value/momentum, FF5+momentum and defensive signal sets (50-100% gross Sharpe improvement, 65% in liquid large caps); same research group, so not independent.
limitations: 130 JKP characteristics, monthly data and 30-year windows versus our 23 inputs, weekly data and 1-8 years of training; gross of costs; no industry neutralization; microcap-driven headline numbers.

claim: AQR Alternative Thinking 2024 Q4 'Can Machines Build Better Stock Portfolios?': complex random-feature models built on economically motivated signals improve out-of-sample gross Sharpe by 50-100% over the simple linear model in three applications (value and momentum; FF5 plus momentum; defensive signals), 65% when restricted to liquid large caps (footnote 17); the complex model's return stream is 'highly additive' to the simple model; adding just two noisy predictors to the value-momentum model cuts performance by about half (Exhibit 7, 1963-2019). Results are gross of transaction costs.
impact_on_spec: Inputs restricted in advance to the 22 economically motivated theme inputs plus size (no alpha101/191, reversal, overnight or news columns); the M0+ML equal blends test the 'additive to simple' claim directly.
independent_replication: None independent; DKKM 2024 is the same group. BSW 2022 is contrary evidence after costs in large caps.
limitations: Practitioner note, hypothetical gross results, long samples since 1963; the cost question is explicitly left open (footnote 11).
quote: Repeating this exercise using only liquid, large cap stocks leads to a 65% Sharpe ratio improvement.

claim: Barroso, Saxena and Wang (Oct 2022, EFMA 2024) 'Calm Your Portfolio': in the 500 largest US stocks, mean-variance portfolios built from improved return forecasts (Fama-MacBeth, feed-forward neural network, conditional autoencoder, IPCA, nonparametric additive models) and improved covariance estimators do not beat the passive value-weighted portfolio after costs; with risk targeting plus turnover penalties all 32 transaction-cost-managed portfolios beat it, and the best net Sharpe ratios (1.10-1.20) come from the linear Fama-MacBeth forecasts with the daily sample covariance, not from the ML forecasts; without short sales none significantly beats the passive strategy.
impact_on_spec: Contrary prior for ML replacing a linear composite after costs in liquid stocks; lowers the prior for M2/M3 replacing M0 and is why the blends M0M2/M0M3 are candidates and why replacement needs the paired test. For v1.3 it is external support for turnover control.
independent_replication: Consistent with Avramov, Cheng and Metzker (2023): ML profits concentrate in microcaps and distressed firms and shrink under economic restrictions.
limitations: Preliminary working paper; 500 largest stocks, monthly mean-variance optimization rather than a rank-weighted beta-hedged book; ML models trained by the authors, not production-grade.
quote: those constructed using combinations of a Fama-MacBeth-based estimator with the daily sample covariance matrix can achieve net-of-costs Sharpe ratios between 1.10 and 1.20

claim: Jensen, Kelly, Malamud and Pedersen (SFI 22-63, 2022 version; RFS 2026): portfolios that put ML return forecasts, risk and trading costs into one objective keep positive out-of-sample net Sharpe ratios, reaching 1.38 for Portfolio-ML for an investor whose wealth reaches $10 billion by 2020, while cost-agnostic Markowitz portfolios fall to negative net returns.
impact_on_spec: Sets the realistic ceiling for a cost-aware book and supports one optimizer holding alpha, risk and costs (design section 8); M3 (random-feature ridge) follows this line. For v1.3 (2026-10-04): eq. (20) 'start from the grown position inherited from last period, and then trade toward an aim portfolio' is the form of rules P2/P3/P2V (drifted tranche weights as the starting point).
independent_replication: Authors' code is public (github theisij/ml-and-the-implementable-efficient-frontier); AQR Alternative Thinking 2024 Q4 reports gains from ML-built stock portfolios; no independent academic replication was read.
limitations: 2022 working-paper version (the RFS 2026 numbers may differ); price-impact costs only; a $10 billion large-cap investor, not a $1M U3000 book; the full model set needs about 75 GB, so we run a reduced version.
